newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to release impounded Montengrin ships.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to release impounded Montengrin ships.

text.p: The United States has agreed that five Montenegrin cargo vessels impounded for the past five years at U.S. ports can be returned to Montenegro, the State Department said Tuesday.
The ships were seized as part of sanctions imposed on rump Yugoslavia during the Bosnian war which ended in late 1995.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the agreement to release them came at a Washington meeting Monday between Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum.

Burns told a news briefing that the process of release was expected to take about three months to enable "notification of other claimants" -- a reference to payment of expenses incurred by the ships during their stay.
Montenegro and Serbia together form the rump Yugoslavia, which was clamped under U.N. sanctions in 1992 because of Serbia's role in fomenting the Bosnian war.
A spokesman for the Montenegrin mission in Washington, Ratko Knezevic, said two of the ships were in New Orleans, one in New York, one in Baltimore and the fifth was believed to be in San Francisco.
He said they were owned by the companies Jugooceanija and Prekokanska Plovidba.
"We really welcome that move by the American government," Knezevic said.
Burns said Kornblum and Djukanovic had "a very constructive exchange of views" in which the U.S. official raised concerns about the need for further democratization in Serbia and Montenegro.

He said the release of the ships did not imply any weakening of what the United States calls its "outer wall" of sanctions still in force against Yugoslavia, including blocking international loans and a U.N. seat.

Washington has set several conditions for lifting those sanctions including Belgrade's cooperation with an international war crimes tribunal and improved treatment of ethnic Albanians in Kosovo province.
